data.narrative:
Impulse Labs is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Sam D'Amico that has raised $25M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of nine private-sector peers in Climate & Energy, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($25M) as a proxy for entry valuation, a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis was not executable; while nine same-sector peers exist, none met the narrow screening criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), falling below the three-datapoint minimum required for reliable median estimation. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with a median point of $50M. This range reflects moderate confidence in the stage-progression method but acknowledges material uncertainty around comparable company financials and the absence of direct peer-matching within Impulse's specific valuation tier. Key risks include the tightness of the applicable method set and potential divergence between raised capital and true entry valuation. Additional peer data or transaction evidence would strengthen conviction materially.
